header.name: NARRATIVES IN VISUAL COMMUNICATION
header.description:
Sharing stories has been the most important way of communication since the early ages of mankind. Cave paintings, books, cinema, more recently an array of digital mediums; all of which are examples of narratives help to communicate, emotional connect, empthise, or even understand ideas, concerns and concepts. According to anthropologist, Mary C. Bateson, "the human species thinks in metaphors and learns through stories." Metaphors help human's to understand abstract concepts. Humans make sense of design through the narrative function of the brain and design uses this connection to create more effectively. Storytelling is a memorable way to communicate ideas with emotional resonance. A story refers to the description provided by a narrative and exhibits a narrative structure and dramatic tension.

Narratives are used in design as a technique to get insight into users, build empathy and access them emotionally. With stories, designers speak to increase the appeal of what they offer and provide a solid understanding of the users. For eg., UX designers typically tell on-screen stories, weaving narratives to make users invest their emotions in our messages. Designers aim to engage users through their feelings, as opposed to describing design of the product or system from a functionalist/task-oriented viewpoint. An effective user experience depends on the success of users’ achieving their goals ‘usability-wise’. However, storytelling is the framework used by designers to reach users. The world can be experienced through metaphors, not bullet-point specifications, storytelling is the best way to relate to audiences. Effective storytelling means going beyond getting users emotionally invested, to keeping them engaged after their experiences, too, so they attach more meaning to designed products/services.

Sketching/Drawing is used as medium both to form a conceptual understanding and execution of narrative as a tool of communication. Sketching/Drawing in Visual Commuication is a fundamental tool for Narratives, which is not limited to using the analogus pencil on paper or the digital tablet and pen. It is an activity that involves observation, visualisation and storytelling.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will enhance their ability to draw and improve upon the quality and speed of their sketching/drawing skills and the ability to think visually.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will develop the ability to deconstruct complex ideas and convey them through visual narratives.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will experiment and explore alternative mediums for storytelling, such as sound, and appropriate technology (eg. the use of online meeting platforms like Zoom, Google Meet etc.)

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will develop the the ability to use narratives as a tool in communication design to connect, engage or interact with users.

21. END TERM PROJECT
The Project must include all the stages of the design process to ensure effective responses to the problem/opportunity area. Following are some of the suggested critical stages (which may be modified to suit the context of the problem/opportunity area):
1. Problem/Opportunity Identification with a Focus on Visual Narratives as an Effective Response to the Problem/Opportunity
2. Research and Scoping of Problem/Opportunity
3. Empathetic Understanding of the User
4. Analysis of Data Collected
5. Exploring Solutions that Responds to the Problem/Opportunity
6. Exploring Narratives and Technology to Respond to the Problem/Opportunity Area
7. Identifying Medium of Communication for the Narrative/s
- Identify a Style that suits the User, Medium and Solution
- Ensure the Narrative encompasses a Structure of a Story
- Textual content to be incorporated with appropriate Fonts
8. Execution of Working Solution with a Focus on Visual Narratives as an Effective Response to the Problem; Lab: CLASS 21. END TERM PROJECT
